title: Signals Notebook vs eLabNext: Which ELN Is Right for Your Lab?
summary: Compare Signals Notebook vs eLabNext across ELN, inventory, integrations, compliance, deployment, and scalability to choose the right platform for your lab.
body_markdown:
## **TL;DR**


- Signals Notebook from Revvity Signals is a cloud-native ELN focused on scientific documentation, collaboration, chemistry workflows, native ChemDraw integration, inventory, and enterprise R&D.
- eLabNext is now part of SciSure and its former capabilities are positioned as SciSure for Research, combining ELN, LIMS, sample tracking, inventory, equipment, and integrations.
- Signals Notebook has a particularly strong chemistry and multidisciplinary R&D focus, while eLabNext emphasizes connected experiments, samples, inventory, equipment, and day-to-day lab operations.
- The right choice depends on research discipline, inventory complexity, LIMS needs, compliance requirements, deployment preferences, integrations, and long-term data strategy.


When comparing **Signals Notebook vs eLabNext** , laboratories are evaluating two established electronic lab notebook platforms with different approaches to research data management.


Signals Notebook centers on cloud-native scientific documentation, chemistry and biology workflows, collaboration, and integrations. eLabNext, now represented within SciSure for Research, extends ELN functionality into sample tracking, inventory, equipment management, LIMS workflows, and an extensible laboratory ecosystem.


## **Signals Notebook vs eLabNext at a Glance**


### **What Is Signals Notebook?**


Signals Notebook is Revvity Signals' cloud-native ELN for pharmaceutical, biotechnology, chemicals, materials, formulation, and other R&D teams.


Its capabilities include:


- Experiment documentation and collaboration
- Native ChemDraw integration
- Microsoft Office integration
- Scientific search
- Inventory and materials management
- Electronic signatures and controlled access
- APIs and instrument integrations
- Connections to broader Signals analytics and AI capabilities


Revvity currently lists Signals Notebook Standard at $1,425 per user annually, while enterprise deployment and validation requirements can involve different editions or commercial terms.


### **What Is eLabNext?**


eLabNext developed an all-in-one Digital Lab Platform combining an ELN with sample, inventory, equipment, and laboratory management capabilities. Its API, SDK, and Marketplace allow laboratories to extend the platform with custom or third-party functionality.


In 2025, eLabNext merged with SciShield to form SciSure. Today, the former eLabNext offering is positioned as SciSure for Research, while the broader SciSure platform combines ELN, LIMS, lab operations, safety, compliance, and integrations.


### **Signals Notebook vs eLabNext: Key Differences**


**Area** **Signals Notebook** **eLabNext / SciSure for Research**


Primary Focus Scientific ELN and R&D collaboration Connected research and lab operations


ELN Core capability Core capability


LIMS Integrates with external LIMS Native LIMS capabilities


Chemistry Native ChemDraw strength General scientific workflows


Inventory Integrated materials management Strong sample and inventory focus


Equipment Integrations and data capture Native equipment management


Extensibility APIs and Signals ecosystem API, SDK, Marketplace add-ons


Deployment Cloud-native, enterprise options Cloud plus dedicated deployment options


## **Signals Notebook vs eLabNext Feature Comparison**


### **Electronic Lab Notebook and Scientific Workflows**


Signals Notebook is built around capturing, organizing, searching, and sharing scientific experiments. Native ChemDraw integration is particularly relevant for medicinal chemistry, synthetic chemistry, formulation, and materials science teams.


Its cloud architecture also supports permission-based collaboration and electronic signatures, while Signals One extends the environment with semantic search, experiment suggestions, protocol optimization, and AI-assisted scientific analysis.


eLabNext takes a broader operational approach. Experiments can connect with samples, inventory, protocols, and equipment, keeping research documentation linked to physical laboratory resources.


Need more than a digital notebook? See how Scispot'sELN software connects experiment records with samples, workflows, and laboratory data.


### **Sample, Inventory, and Equipment Management**


This is an important distinction in the comparison.


Signals Notebook includes materials and inventory functionality and can connect scientific records with reagents and experimental materials.


eLabNext has historically placed stronger emphasis on integrated sample, inventory, and equipment management alongside its ELN. Its platform was designed so researchers could connect physical materials and lab resources directly to experimental records.


The current SciSure platform extends this concept further by connecting research documentation, sample tracking, inventory, lab operations, and safety workflows.


### **Integrations and Instrument Connectivity**


Signals Notebook supports APIs that allow external applications to write instrument data into experiments or retrieve information from systems such as LIMS platforms and external databases.


eLabNext provides API and SDK access through its developer environment, while its Marketplace allows teams to add integrations and custom functionality. SciSure continues to support integrations with instruments, software, and external systems.


For laboratories where connectivity is a major selection criterion, Scispot's[laboratory integration platform](https://www.scispot.com/integrations) connects instruments, ELNs, LIMS, databases, and cloud applications.


If integration maintenance is consuming scientific or IT time, Scispot can automate laboratory data movement and standardization across your stack.


### **Compliance and Deployment**


Signals Notebook supports permission management, electronic approvals, audit controls, and 21 CFR Part 11-oriented deployments. Revvity also offers validation-ready enterprise configurations for regulated environments.


SciSure for Research supports structured, version-controlled experiment records and positions its research platform for regulated and GxP-oriented environments. Dedicated private cloud and on-premises configurations continue to receive scheduled product updates.


Regulated buyers should validate the exact deployment, electronic signature, validation package, change-control, and SOP requirements for their intended use.


## **Which Labs Should Consider Signals Notebook or eLabNext?**


### **Chemistry and Pharmaceutical R&D Teams**


Signals Notebook is particularly relevant where ChemDraw, chemical structures, scientific collaboration, analytical data, and multidisciplinary R&D workflows are central.


Scispot's[Benchling vs Signals Notebook comparison](https://www.scispot.com/blog/benchling-vs-signals-notebook) provides another view of its positioning for enterprise research teams.


### **Biotech and Research Labs Managing Physical Resources**


eLabNext, now SciSure for Research, may be relevant when the ELN needs to stay closely connected with samples, inventory, equipment, protocols, and day-to-day laboratory management.


Teams evaluating this category can also review Scispot's[Benchling vs eLabNext comparison](https://www.scispot.com/blog/benchling-vs-elabnext) .


### **Labs That Need ELN and LIMS Together**


If sample lifecycle management, operational workflows, approvals, instruments, and experiment records all need to work together, buyers should evaluate whether an ELN-centered architecture is sufficient or whether they need a broader laboratory operating platform.


### **Key Questions to Ask Before Choosing**


During vendor demos, test:


- How experiments connect to samples and inventory
- Whether workflows can be changed without vendor development
- Instrument integration and API coverage
- Data export and portability
- Electronic signatures and audit trails
- Deployment and validation requirements
- Administration effort as the lab scales
- AI access to structured scientific data


For a broader shortlist, Scispot's guide to[eLabNext alternatives and competitors](https://www.scispot.com/blog/top-elabnext-alternatives-and-competitors) covers additional platforms for research laboratories.
